messages.author: 3a5ecc9a7eeb64b1
messages.subject: Problem fitting multistate multinomial model
parts:
Hi all, 

I am trying to fit a multistate multinomial model, where I look at the movement from state A to state B (susceptible to infected), with survival as a fixed effect, detection probability as a random effect, movement from state A. Now that I have changed to a time varying model, I am having problems setting my initial values and I get the following error:

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 
  3 nodes produced errors; first error: RUNTIME ERROR:
Dimension mismatch in values supplied for psiAB

I am sure I am missing something obvious - any help is much appreciated!

Thanks, Luci

#Model

###############################################

# 2. Approach: multinomial likelihood

# 2.1. Specify model in BUGS language
cat(file = "multinom-ms1.jags", "
model {

# -------------------------------------------------
# Parameters:
# phiA: survival probability in state A
# phiB: survival probability in state B
# psiAB: movement probability from state A to state B
# psiBA: movement probability from state B to state A
# pA: recapture probability at state A
# pB: recapture probability at state B
# -------------------------------------------------

# Priors and constraints
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
   phiA[t] ~ dunif(0, 1)
   phiB[t] ~ dunif(0, 1) #constant over time for all of these. Where yo change for eg temporal random / fixed effects
   psiAB[t] ~ dunif(0, 1)
   psiBA[t] <- 0
   logit(pA[t]) <- logit(mean.p[1]) + epsilon[t] 
   logit(pB[t]) <- logit(mean.p[2]) + epsilon[t] 
   epsilon[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau)

   
   }

  for (u in 1:2){
   mean.p[u] ~ dunif(0, 1)      # Priors for mean state-spec. recapture
   }

  #Priors for random effects
  sigma ~ dunif(0, 10)                      # Prior for standard deviation
  tau <- pow(sigma, -2)
  sigma2 <- pow(sigma, 2)                  # Temporal variance
  

# Define state-transition and reencounter probabilities - note no i index - is no longer individual 
   for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
      psi[1,t,1] <- phiA[t] * (1-psiAB[t])
      psi[1,t,2] <- phiA[t] * psiAB[t]
      psi[2,t,1] <- phiB[t] * psiBA[t]
      psi[2,t,2] <- phiB[t] * (1-psiBA[t])

      po[1,t] <- pA[t]
      po[2,t] <- pB[t]


      # Calculate probability of non-encounter (dq) and reshape the array for the encounter probabilities - below here says the same     
      for (s in 1:ns){
         dp[s,t,s] <- po[s,t]
         dq[s,t,s] <- 1-po[s,t]
         } # s
      for (s in 1:(ns-1)){
         for (m in (s+1):ns){
            dp[s,t,m] <- 0
            dq[s,t,m] <- 0
            } # s
         } # m
      for (s in 2:ns){
         for (m in 1:(s-1)){
            dp[s,t,m] <- 0
            dq[s,t,m] <- 0
            } # s
         } # m
      } # t

# Define the multinomial likelihood
for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*ns)){
   marr[t,1:(n.occasions*ns-(ns-1))] ~ dmulti(pr[t,], rel[t])
   }

# Define the cell probabilities of the multistate m-array   
# Define matrix U: product of probabilities of state-transition and non-encounter (this is just done because there is no product function for matrix multiplication in JAGS)
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){
   U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns), (t-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- ones
   for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){
      U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns), (j-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns), (j-2)*ns+(1:ns)] %*% psi[,t,] %*% dq[,t,]
      }
   }
U[(n.occasions-2)*ns+(1:ns), (n.occasions-2)*ns+(1:ns)] <- ones
# Diagonal
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){
   pr[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(t-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(t-1)*ns+(1:ns)] %*% psi[,t,] %*% dp[,t,]
   # Above main diagonal
   for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){
      pr[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns), (j-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns), (j-1)*ns+(1:ns)] %*% psi[,j,] %*% dp[,j,]
      }
   }
pr[(n.occasions-2)*ns+(1:ns), (n.occasions-2)*ns+(1:ns)] <- psi[,n.occasions-1,] %*% dp[,n.occasions-1,]

# Below main diagonal
for (t in 2:(n.occasions-1)){
   for (j in 1:(t-1)){
      pr[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(j-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- zero
      } #j
   } #t

# Last column: probability of non-recapture
for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*ns)){
   pr[t,(n.occasions*ns-(ns-1))] <- 1-sum(pr[t,1:((n.occasions-1)*ns)])
   } #t
}
")


marray <- function(ch, unobs = 0){
   ns <- length(table(ch)) - 1 + unobs
   no <- ncol(ch)
   out <- matrix(0, ncol = ns*(no-1)+1, nrow = ns*(no-1))
   # Remove capture histories of individuals that are marked at last occasion
   get.first <- function(x) min(which(x!=0))
   first <- apply(ch, 1, get.first)
   last.only <- which(first==no)
   if (length(last.only) > 0) ch <- ch[-last.only,]
   # Compute m-array
   for (i in 1:nrow(ch)){
      cap.occ <- which(ch[i,]!=0)
      state <- ch[i,cap.occ]
      if (length(state) == 1) {
         out[state[1]+ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[state[1]+ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] + 1
         }
      if (length(state) > 1) {
         for (t in 2:length(cap.occ)){
            out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*ns+state[t]] <- out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*ns+state[t]] + 1
            } # t
         if (max(cap.occ) < no){
            out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] + 1
            } # if
         } # if
      } # t
   return(out)
   }    

# Create multistate m-array
ms.arr <- marray(ch)

# Calculate the number of states
ns <- length(unique(as.numeric(ch))) - 1

# Bundle data
jags.data <- list(marr = ms.arr, n.occasions = ncol(ch), rel = rowSums(ms.arr), ns = ns, zero = matrix(0, ncol = ns, nrow = ns), ones = diag(ns))

marr<-ms.arr

# 2.3. Initial values - think this is where my problem is

inits <- function(){list(phiA = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1),phiB = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1),psiAB = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1))}  

inits <- function(){list(psiAB = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1))}  



# 2.4. Parameters monitored
parameters <- c("phiA", "phiB", "psiAB", "psiBA", "mean.p")

# 2.5. MCMC settings
ni <- 4000; nt <- 1; nb <- 2000; nc <- 3

# 2.6. Call JAGS from R
m.ms_2 <- jags(jags.data,inits,  parameters, "multinom-ms1.jags", n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, parallel = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Problem fitting multistate multinomial model
parts:
Hi Lucinda,

I haven't fully delved into your code, but in my experience, this error usually indicates that your inits don't match your model in terms of the dimensions of the object in question (in this case, psiAB). For example, this might happen if you specify a vector in the inits but then try to use the object as a matrix in the model; or if your object is initialized as a vector with length N, but then you try to refer to a position greater than N in the vector within the model. In this case, I'm not sure if dim(marr)[2]-1 will equal n.occasions-1 - but if so, what I've described probably isn't your problem, unless I've missed something.

I also noticed that you've specified the "inits" object twice - could that be a problem?

inits <- function(){list(phiA = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1),phiB = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1),psiAB = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1))}  

inits <- function(){list(psiAB = runif(dim(marr)[2]-1, 0, 1))}

I guess psiAB is specified identically in both of them, so perhaps that doesn't explain why there is an error relating to psiAB. But phiA and phiB are missing in the second line (which is what will beused) so maybe that has some downstream effects...?

If that doesn't help, I'll take a closer look later, or perhaps someone else will beat me to it.

Cheers,

Emily

      }
   }

   pr[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(t-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(t-1)*ns+(1:ns)] %*% psi[,t,] %*% dp[,t,]

marray <- function(ch, unobs = 0){
   ns <- length(table(ch)) - 1 + unobs
   no <- ncol(ch)
   out <- matrix(0, ncol = ns*(no-1)+1, nrow = ns*(no-1))
   # Remove capture histories of individuals that are marked at last occasion
   get.first <- function(x) min(which(x!=0))
   first <- apply(ch, 1, get.first)
   last.only <- which(first==no)
   if (length(last.only) > 0) ch <- ch[-last.only,]
   # Compute m-array
   for (i in 1:nrow(ch)){
      cap.occ <- which(ch[i,]!=0)
      state <- ch[i,cap.occ]
      if (length(state) == 1) {
         out[state[1]+ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[state[1]+ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] + 1
         }
      if (length(state) > 1) {
         for (t in 2:length(cap.occ)){
            out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*ns+state[t]] <- out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*ns+state[t]] + 1
            } # t
         if (max(cap.occ) < no){
            out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] + 1
            } # if
         } # if
      } # t
   return(out)
   }    

# Create multistate m-array
ms.arr <- marray(ch)

# Calculate the number of states
ns <- length(unique(as.numeric(ch))) - 1

# Bundle data
jags.data <- list(marr = ms.arr, n.occasions = ncol(ch), rel = rowSums(ms.arr), ns = ns, zero = matrix(0, ncol = ns, nrow = ns), ones = diag(ns))
